research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
within-team variation in role coverage across lineups
separability of role coverage from player talent and playing-time counts
talent control in lineup-level influence models
methodological_questions: Is lineup role coverage separable from talent and playing-time counts once talent is controlled?
Does talent control behave as intended for role-coverage measures derived from play-by-play?
Do role labels derived from play-by-play (initiator, play type, points) leak outcome information into the coverage measure?
What confounding, reliability, and exposure risks threaten lineup-level role-coverage tests?
evidence_establishes: No earlier study from this project was returned by retrieve_history for this question, so no prior finding on lineup role coverage, its separability, or talent control is established by the retrieved record.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether organizer, shaper, or terminal coverage varies within team in these data.
Whether role coverage carries information beyond talent and counts.
Whether the talent-control procedure is valid for these measures.
Any effect size, direction, or reliability for role coverage.
own_inferences: The question is only partly testable: within-team variation in coverage can be described directly from the play-by-play-derived possession records, but the separability and talent-control claims require a model with a talent measure that is not itself built from the same possessions.
Role labels built from initiator and play-type fields that also carry points risk making coverage partly a function of scoring outcomes, so the outcome and the role measure may not be independent.
With 90 team-seasons, team-level estimates of talent and coverage will be noisy; lineup-level estimates will be sparse for many combinations, so shrinkage or pooling will be needed.
Playoff games are a much smaller sample and may serve as a holdout for transfer checks rather than as a primary test.
uncertainties: No historical records were returned, so no earlier attempts, failures, or validated role definitions are known.
The exact definitions of organizer, shaper, and terminal, and how they are assigned from play types, are not given in the task statement.
The talent measure to be used for control is not specified; if it is derived from the same play-by-play, the control may absorb part of the coverage effect.
The number of lineups with adequate possessions per team-season is unknown.
Whether the 2025-26 regular season and playoffs, both complete by the stated question date, are stable with respect to earlier seasons is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned an empty list, so no prior study, failed approach, or validated measure was available to change the decision. The decision rests on the task statement and the data description alone.

blocking_constraints.text: Role assignments built from play types and points may encode the same scoring outcome that the influence measure reports, so coverage and outcome are not independent.
Lineup role coverage is correlated with player talent, usage, and minutes; separability depends on a talent measure that is not derived from the same possessions.
Many lineup combinations will have few possessions within a team-season, limiting within-team contrasts in coverage.
With 90 team-seasons, power to detect a modest coverage effect after talent and count control is likely limited.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was returned by retrieve_history, so it is unknown whether this question, or a close version of it, has already been answered. No prior work is relied on.

risks.text: Organizer, shaper, and terminal labels derived from play type and points may partly encode scoring; coverage must be defined from pre-outcome action fields, or outcome-free labels must be checked.

If a lineup's role coverage is computed over the same possessions used to score the lineup, the coverage-outcome association is inflated by construction; roles must be computed from data that precede the outcome window.
Usage, minutes, and talent co-vary with role coverage; a talent measure built from the same play-by-play may over-control or under-control the coverage effect.
Coaches choose lineups in response to game state and performance, so coverage levels selected for high-leverage stints are not random.
Role coverage measured from one or two seasons per lineup may have low split-half reliability, which attenuates separability tests.
Lineup-level estimates with few possessions are unstable; within-team coverage contrasts may rest on very few lineups per team-season.
Ninety team-seasons give limited power for interaction or incremental-R² tests of coverage beyond talent and counts.
Three roles, a composite coverage index, and several talent controls create many tests that need correction.
If talent control is weak, a placebo role (e.g., a shuffled or non-structural action category) may show a similar association, so the placebo must be shown to be null.
Rule changes, pace, and three-point volume shifts across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may change role frequencies over time; season effects must be modelled.
Play-by-play action and sub-type mapping to roles may be misclassified, especially for ambiguous possessions; a label audit is needed.
Joins between play-by-play, substitution intervals, and the graph-derived possession records may misalign lineups or stints; reconciliation checks are required.
If one role is rare in most lineups, coverage will be near-constant and contrasts will be uninformative.

design.estimand: Incremental association of within-team lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper, and terminal present) with lineup-stint offensive and net efficiency, after controlling for a talent measure built independently of the outcome window and for minutes and possession counts; plus the variance in coverage not explained by talent and counts.
design.unit: Lineup stint (five-player unit within a team-game) nested in team-season; role coverage is a binary indicator per role and a count index.
design.sample: NBA regular seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 (2025-26 regular season complete as of 2026-04-13), with playoffs 2022-23 to 2025-26 (2025-26 playoffs complete as of 2026-06-21) used as a held-out transfer check; 420,993 possessions across 90 team-seasons, restricted to lineups above a pre-specified possession threshold.
design.power: Power must be computed before analysis via simulation over the observed lineup-possession distribution; the target is detection of a pre-specified incremental effect at 80% power with a two-sided alpha of 0.05 after multiplicity correction. If simulated power is below 80%, the claim is restricted to descriptive variation.
design.controls: Talent control from an independent source (e.g., prior-season box-score or a shrunk player-level estimate computed from disjoint possessions); minutes and possession counts; team-season and season fixed effects; opponent strength; game state (score margin, period, garbage time exclusion); role coverage computed only from actions preceding the scored possession to avoid leakage; cross-fitted talent estimates.
design.falsification: Placebo role labels built from non-structural action categories or shuffled within lineup must show no incremental association; a talent-only model must reproduce the coverage association if it is merely talent; an outcome-free role definition must replicate the main estimate; playoff-sample transfer must hold in direction.
design.multiplicity: Holm correction across the three role indicators and the composite index; a separate pre-specified primary test (composite coverage, talent-controlled) with other tests treated as secondary.
design.decision_rule: Claim supported only if the primary composite coverage coefficient, after talent and count controls, has a 95% cluster-robust interval excluding zero in the regular-season sample, the placebo coefficient interval includes zero, the outcome-free definition replicates in sign, and the playoff transfer keeps the sign. Otherwise report uncertain or rejected, following the power check.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs, with 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21), frozen at the question date of 2026-07-13; graph-derived play-type possession records built from the same play-by-play.

You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
